Here is a basic example of how you could write a Semgrep rule for this vulnerability:

```yaml
rules:
  - id: "vuln-mcp-server-taskwarrior-1ee3d282"
    pattern: |
      execSync(`task ${parsed.data.identifier} done`, { maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024 * 10 })
    languages: ["typescript"]
    message: "Potential command injection vulnerability in Taskwarrior"
    severity: ERROR
    metadata:
      source-url: https://github.com/awwaiid/mcp-server-taskwarrior/commit/1ee3d282debfa0a99afeb41d22c4b2fd5a3148f2
      category: security
      cwe: CWE-78
      owasp: A6
      references: https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Command_Injection, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-1324
```

This rule will match any usage of `execSync` with a command string that includes `${parsed.data.identifier}`. It's important to note that this is a very basic example and might not cover all possible variations of the vulnerability. You should adjust it according to your specific needs.
